sanskrit: śuka uvāca vartamānas tathaivātra vānaprasthāśrame yathā yoktavyo ''tmā yathā śaktyā paraṃ vai kāṅkṣatā padam
english: Śuka said: While dwelling within the order of the forest-hermit, how should one who longs, to the utmost of his power, for the supreme station discipline his own self?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca prāpya saṃskāram etābhyām āśramābhyāṃ tataḥ param yat kāryaṃ paramārthārthaṃ tad ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: Vyāsa said: Having gained, through these two orders of life, his consecration, hear now with single-minded attention what task remains to be done thereafter, for the sake of the supreme end.

sanskrit: kaṣāyaṃ pācayitvā tu śreṇisthāneṣu ca triṣu pravrajec ca paraṃ sthānaṃ parivrajyām anuttamām
english: Having burned away the dross within the three graded stations, let him go forth into the supreme station, the unsurpassed wandering life of renunciation.

sanskrit: tad bhavān evam abhyasya vartatāṃ śrūyatāṃ tathā eka eva caren nityaṃ siddhyartham asahāyavān
english: Practising thus, let your honoured self abide therein, and hear how it is done: ever alone, without companion, let him wander for the sake of perfection.

sanskrit: ekaś carati yaḥ paśyan na jahāti na hīyate anagnir aniketaḥ syād grāmam annārtham āśrayet
english: He who wanders alone, keeping watch, neither forsakes nor is forsaken. Let him be without sacred fire and without fixed abode, and resort to a village only to seek his food.

sanskrit: aśvastanavidhānaḥ syān munir bhāvasamanvitaḥ laghvāśī niyatāhāraḥ sakṛd annaniṣevitā
english: Let the sage make no provision for the morrow, filled with inward feeling; eating sparingly, restrained in his food, partaking of a meal but once.

sanskrit: kapālaṃ vṛkṣamūlāni kucelam asahāyatā upekṣā sarvabhūtānām etāvad bhikṣulakṣaṇam
english: A begging bowl, the roots of trees for shelter, ragged clothing, solitude, and indifference toward all creatures—this much is the mark of the mendicant.

sanskrit: yasmin vācaḥ praviśanti kūpe prāptāḥ śilā iva na vaktāraṃ punar yānti sa kaivalyāśrame vaset
english: He into whom words enter as stones dropped into a well, never returning to their speaker, may dwell in the order of absolute aloneness.

sanskrit: naiva paśyen na śṛṇuyād avācyaṃ jātu kasya cit brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣeṇa naiva brūyāt kathaṃ cana
english: Let him neither see nor hear anything unfit to be spoken of anyone whatever, and above all let him never in any way speak ill of the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: yad brāhmaṇasya kuśalaṃ tad eva satataṃ vadet tūṣṇīm āsīta nindāyāṃ kurvan bheṣajam ātmanaḥ
english: Whatever is for a brāhmaṇa's welfare, that alone let him constantly speak; when reviled, let him sit silent, thereby making a medicine for his own soul.

sanskrit: yena pūrṇam ivākāśaṃ bhavaty ekena sarvadā śūnyaṃ yena janākīrṇaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: He by whom alone the empty sky seems forever full, and by whom a place thronged with people seems void—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: yena kena cid ācchanno yena kena cid āśitaḥ yatrakvacanaśāyī ca taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: Covered with whatever comes to hand, fed by whatever comes to hand, lying down to sleep wherever he may be—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: aher iva gaṇād bhītaḥ sauhityān narakād iva kuṇapād iva ca strībhyas taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: He who shrinks from a crowd as from a serpent, from sated fullness as from hell, and from women as from a corpse—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: na krudhyen na prahṛṣyec ca mānito 'mānitaś ca yaḥ sarvabhūteṣv abhayadas taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: He who, whether honoured or dishonoured, neither flares in anger nor swells with delight, and who grants safety to all creatures—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: nābhinandeta maraṇaṃ nābhinandeta jīvitam kālam eva pratīkṣeta nideśaṃ bhṛtako yathā
english: Let him not welcome death, nor welcome life; let him only await his time, as a hired servant awaits his orders.

sanskrit: anabhyāhatacittaḥ syād anabhyāhatavāk tathā nirmuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo niramitrasya kiṃ bhayam
english: Let his mind be unassailed and his speech likewise unassailing; released from all sins, having no enemy, what fear can be his?

sanskrit: abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo bhūtānām abhayaṃ yataḥ tasya dehād vimuktasya bhayaṃ nāsti kutaś cana
english: Since from him all creatures have nothing to fear, and he in turn has nothing to fear from any creature, for him who is freed from the body there is no fear from any quarter.

sanskrit: yathā nāgapade 'nyāni padāni padagāminām sarvāṇy evāpidhīyante padajātāni kauñjare
english: As within the footprint of the elephant the footprints of all other creatures that walk are wholly contained,

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvam ahiṃsāyāṃ dharmārtham apidhīyate amṛtaḥ sa nityaṃ vasati yo 'hiṃsāṃ pratipadyate
english: so within non-injury the whole of righteousness's purpose is contained; immortal forever dwells the man who takes up the practice of non-injury.

sanskrit: ahiṃsakaḥ samaḥ satyo dhṛtimān niyatendriyaḥ śaraṇyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ gatim āpnoty anuttamām
english: Harmless, even-minded, truthful, steadfast, his senses curbed, a refuge to all creatures, he attains the unsurpassed goal.

sanskrit: evaṃ prajñānatṛptasya nirbhayasya manīṣiṇaḥ na mṛtyur atigo bhāvaḥ sa mṛtyum adhigacchati
english: For the sage thus contented in wisdom and free of fear, death is not a state beyond his reach; rather, he overtakes death itself.

sanskrit: vimuktaṃ sarvasaṅgebhyo munim ākāśavat sthitam asvam ekacaraṃ śāntaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: The sage released from all attachments, standing firm like the open sky, owning nothing, wandering alone, at peace—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: jīvitaṃ yasya dharmārthaṃ dharmo 'ratyartham eva ca ahorātrāś ca puṇyārthaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: He whose life is for the sake of righteousness, whose righteousness is for the sake of detachment, and whose days and nights are for the sake of merit—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: nirāśiṣam anārambhaṃ nirnamaskāram astutim akṣīṇaṃ kṣīṇakarmāṇaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ
english: Free of craving, undertaking nothing, neither bowed to nor praised, undiminished though his works are spent—him the gods know to be a true brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi bhūtāni sukhe ramante; sarvāṇi duḥkhasya bhṛśaṃ trasanti teṣāṃ bhayotpādanajātakhedaḥ; kuryān na karmāṇi hi śraddadhānaḥ
english: All creatures delight in happiness; all shrink in dread from pain. Grieved at the thought of causing them fear, the man of faith should do no deeds that breed it.

sanskrit: dānaṃ hi bhūtābhayadakṣiṇāyāḥ; sarvāṇi dānāny adhitiṣṭhatīha tīkṣṇāṃ tanuṃ yaḥ prathamaṃ jahāti; so 'nantam āpnoty abhayaṃ prajābhyaḥ
english: The gift whose offering is freedom from fear to all beings surpasses every other gift here below; and he who first lays aside his fierce, cruel nature wins from all creatures a boundless freedom from fear.

sanskrit: uttāna āsyena havir juhoti; lokasya nābhir jagataḥ pratiṣṭhā tasyāṅgam aṅgāni kṛtākṛtaṃ ca; vaiśvānaraḥ sarvam eva prapede
english: Lying upturned, with mouth he pours the oblation—he, the navel of the world, the world's foundation; his limbs are all things, the done and the undone alike, for the All-Pervading Fire has entered into everything.

sanskrit: prādeśamātre hṛdi niśritaṃ yat; tasmin prāṇān ātmayājī juhoti tasyāgnihotraṃ hutam ātmasaṃsthaṃ; sarveṣu lokeṣu sadaivateṣu
english: Into that which rests within the heart, a mere span in measure, the self-sacrificer pours his life-breaths as oblation; his fire-offering, poured and grounded in the Self, reaches through all the worlds together with their gods.

sanskrit: daivaṃ tridhātuṃ trivṛtaṃ suparṇaṃ; ye vidyur agryaṃ paramārthatāṃ ca te sarvalokeṣu mahīyamānā; devāḥ samarthāḥ sukṛtaṃ vrajanti
english: Those who know the divine, threefold in substance, triply enfolded, fair-winged and foremost, and who know its supreme reality—they, honoured in all the worlds, mighty as gods, pass on to the abode of the well-doer.

sanskrit: vedāṃś ca vedyaṃ ca vidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam; atho niruktaṃ paramārthatāṃ ca sarvaṃ śarīrātmani yaḥ praveda; tasmai sma devāḥ spṛhayanti nityam
english: He who knows the Vedas, the object of knowledge, the ordinance entire, the etymology, and the supreme reality—who knows all this as seated in the Self within the body—for him the gods forever yearn.

sanskrit: bhūmāv asaktaṃ divi cāprameyaṃ; hiraṇmayaṃ yo 'ṇḍajam aṇḍamadhye patatriṇaṃ pakṣiṇam antarikṣe; yo veda bhogyātmani dīptaraśmiḥ
english: Unattached to the earth, immeasurable in heaven, golden, egg-born within the cosmic egg—he who knows that winged one, the bird soaring in the midspace, knows it as the radiant-rayed enjoyer within the Self that is enjoyed.

sanskrit: āvartamānam ajaraṃ vivartanaṃ; ṣaṇṇemikaṃ dvādaśāraṃ suparva yasyedam āsye pariyāti viśvaṃ; tat kālacakraṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām
english: Revolving, ageless, ever-turning, with six fellies, twelve spokes, and goodly joints—within whose mouth the whole universe wheels round—that is the wheel of Time, set hidden in the cave of the heart.

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃprasādaṃ jagataḥ śarīraṃ; sarvān sa lokān adhigacchatīha tasmin hutaṃ tarpayatīha devāṃs; te vai tṛptās tarpayanty āsyam asya
english: He who knows the serene radiance to be the body of the world attains here to all the worlds; what is offered into it gratifies the gods, and they, gratified in turn, gratify his mouth.

sanskrit: tejomayo nityatanuḥ purāṇo; lokān anantān abhayān upaiti bhūtāni yasmān na trasante kadā cit; sa bhūtebhyo na trasate kadā cit
english: Made of splendour, of eternal frame, ancient, he passes to the worlds that are endless and free of fear; he of whom creatures never stand in dread is himself never in dread of creatures.

sanskrit: agarhaṇīyo na ca garhate 'nyān; sa vai vipraḥ paramātmānam īkṣet vinītamoho vyapanītakalmaṣo; na ceha nāmutra ca yo 'rtham ṛcchati
english: Himself beyond blame, and blaming no other—that sage may behold the supreme Self; his delusion subdued, his stain washed away, he seeks no gain either here or hereafter.

sanskrit: aroṣamohaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanaḥ; prahīṇaśoko gatasaṃdhivigrahaḥ apetanindāstutir apriyāpriyaś; carann udāsīnavad eṣa bhikṣukaḥ
english: Free of wrath and delusion, holding a clod and gold as equal, his grief abandoned, beyond alliance and enmity, beyond blame and praise, indifferent to the loved and the unloved—such a mendicant wanders as one wholly detached.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca prakṛtes tu vikārā ye kṣetrajñas taiḥ pariśritaḥ te cainaṃ na prajānanti sa tu jānāti tān api
english: Vyāsa said: The knower of the field is surrounded by the modifications of Nature; yet they do not know him, while he indeed knows them all.

sanskrit: taiś caiṣa kurute kāryaṃ manaḥṣaṣṭhair ihendriyaiḥ sudāntair iva saṃyantā dṛḍhaiḥ paramavājibhiḥ
english: Through them—through the senses, with the mind as the sixth—he accomplishes his work, like a charioteer guiding strong and well-broken steeds of the finest breed.

sanskrit: indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaḥ paramaṃ manaḥ manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ
english: Higher than the senses are their objects; higher than the objects is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the great Self.

sanskrit: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt parato 'mṛtam amṛtān na paraṃ kiṃ cit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ
english: Higher than the great is the Unmanifest; higher than the Unmanifest is the Immortal; than the Immortal there is nothing higher—that is the limit, that the supreme goal.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho ''tmā na prakāśate dṛśyate tvagryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā tattvadarśibhiḥ
english: Thus the Self, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth; yet it is seen by those who perceive the truth, through a keen and subtle intellect.

sanskrit: antarātmani saṃlīya manaḥṣaṣṭhāni medhayā indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃś ca bahu cintyam acintayan
english: Dissolving by his wisdom into the inner Self the senses, with the mind as the sixth, together with the objects of sense, and ceasing to brood upon the manifold matters of thought—

sanskrit: dhyānoparamaṇaṃ kṛtvā vidyāsaṃpāditaṃ manaḥ anīśvaraḥ praśāntātma tato 'rchaty amṛtaṃ padam
english: having brought meditation to its rest, his mind perfected by knowledge, owning no lord, his self wholly tranquil, he then attains the immortal station.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ vaśyātmā calitasmṛtiḥ ātmanaḥ saṃpradānena martyo mṛtyum upāśnute
english: But the mortal who, while mastering all his senses, is shaken in his recollection, by the surrender of his self comes only to death.

sanskrit: hitvā tu sarvasaṃkalpān sattve cittaṃ niveśayet sattve cittaṃ samāveśya tataḥ kālaṃjaro bhavet
english: But casting off all his wilful imaginings, let him fix his thought in purity; and having fixed his thought in purity, he becomes thereby a conqueror of time.

sanskrit: cittaprasādena yatir jahāti hi śubhāśubham prasannātmātmani sthitvā sukham ānantyam aśnute
english: By the serenity of his thought the ascetic forsakes both good and evil; serene of self, abiding in the Self, he wins the happiness that is without end.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ tu prasādasya yathā tṛptaḥ sukhaṃ svapet nivāte vā yathā dīpo dīpyamāno na kampate
english: The mark of that serenity is this: as a contented man sleeps happily, or as a lamp that burns in a windless place does not flicker.

sanskrit: evaṃ pūrvāpare rātre yuñjann ātmānam ātmanā sattvāhāraviśuddhātmā paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: Thus joining the self to the Self in the first and the last watches of the night, his being purified by sattvic food, he beholds the Self within the self.

sanskrit: rahasyaṃ sarvavedānām anaitihyam anāgamam ātmapratyayikaṃ śāstram idaṃ putrānuśāsanam
english: This teaching, the secret of all the Vedas, resting on no mere tradition and no external scripture but on the soul's own conviction—this is the instruction I give to my son.

sanskrit: dharmākhyāneṣu sarveṣu satyākhyāneṣu yad vasu daśedam ṛk sahasrāṇi nirmathyāmṛtam uddhṛtam
english: Whatever treasure lies in all discourses on righteousness and in all discourses on truth—this nectar has been churned forth and drawn up out of ten thousand ṛc-verses.

sanskrit: navanītaṃ yathā dadhnaḥ kāṣṭhād agnir yathaiva ca tathaiva viduṣāṃ jñānaṃ putrahetoḥ samuddhṛtam snātakānām idaṃ śāstraṃ vācyaṃ putrānuśāsanam
english: As butter is drawn from curd, as fire is drawn from wood, so has the wisdom of the learned been drawn forth for the sake of a son. This teaching, this instruction to a son, is to be spoken to those who have completed their studies.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ nāpraśāntāya nādāntāyātapasvine nāvedaviduṣe vācyaṃ tathā nānugatāya ca
english: It is not to be told to one who is unquiet, nor to the unrestrained, nor to one without austerity, nor to one ignorant of the Vedas, nor to one who is not a devoted follower.

sanskrit: nāsūyakāyānṛjave na cānirdiṣṭakāriṇe na tarkaśāstradagdhāya tathaiva piśunāya ca
english: Not to the envious, not to the crooked, not to one who acts contrary to instruction, not to one scorched by the science of mere argument, nor likewise to the slanderer.

sanskrit: ślāghate ślāghanīyāya praśāntāya tapasvine idaṃ priyāya putrāya śiṣyāyānugatāya ca rahasyadharmaṃ vaktavyaṃ nānyasmai tu kathaṃ cana
english: To one worthy of praise who praises rightly, to the tranquil, to the man of austerity, to a beloved son, to a devoted pupil who follows faithfully—to such a one this secret of righteousness is to be told, but to no other in any wise.

sanskrit: yady apy asya mahīṃ dadyād ratnapūrṇām imāṃ naraḥ idam eva tataḥ śreya iti manyeta tattvavit
english: Even should a man offer him this whole earth filled with jewels, the knower of truth would still hold this teaching to be the better thing of the two.

sanskrit: ato guhyatarārthaṃ tad adhyātmam atimānuṣam yat tan maharṣibhir dṛṣṭaṃ vedānteṣu ca gīyate tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: Therefore that knowledge of the supreme Self, more hidden in meaning, more than human, which the great seers have beheld and which is sung in the Vedānta—that I shall now declare to you, even as you question me.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca adhyātmaṃ vistareṇeha punar eva vadasva me yad adhyātmaṃ yathā cedaṃ bhagavann ṛṣisattama
english: Śuka said: Speak to me yet again, and at length, of the knowledge of the Self—what this knowledge of the Self is, and how it stands, O blessed one, O best of seers.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca adhyātmaṃ yad idaṃ tāta puruṣasyeha vidyate tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi tasya vyākhyām imāṃ śṛṇu
english: Vyāsa said: This knowledge of the Self, my son, as it is found in man here below—that I shall declare to you; hear now this its exposition.

sanskrit: bhūmir āpas tathā jyotir vāyur ākāśam eva ca mahābhūtāni bhūtānāṃ sāgarasyormayo yathā
english: Earth, water, fire, wind, and likewise space—these are the great elements of created beings, as the waves are of the sea.

sanskrit: prasāryeha yathāṅgāni kūrmaḥ saṃharate punaḥ tadvan mahānti bhūtāni yavīyaḥsu vikurvate
english: As the tortoise stretches forth its limbs here and again draws them in, so the great elements take on their transformations within the lesser beings.

sanskrit: iti tanmayam evedaṃ sarvaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam sarge ca pralaye caiva tasmān nirdiśyate tathā
english: Thus this whole world of things moving and unmoving is made of those very elements, both in its creation and in its dissolution; and therefore it is so declared.

sanskrit: mahābhūtāni pañcaiva sarvabhūteṣu bhūtakṛt akarot tāta vaiṣamyaṃ yasmin yad anupaśyati
english: The Maker of beings, my son, fashioned the five great elements within all creatures, and wrought in them the diversity wherein each perceives its own nature.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca akarod yac charīreṣu kathaṃ tad upalakṣayet indriyāṇi guṇāḥ ke cit kathaṃ tān upalakṣayet
english: Śuka said: That which he wrought within bodies—how is it to be discerned? And which qualities belong to the senses—how are these to be discerned?

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca etat te vartayiṣyāmi yathāvad iha darśanam śṛṇu tattvam ihaikāgro yathātattvaṃ yathā ca tat
english: Vyāsa said: This I shall set forth to you, the doctrine even as it is; hear with single mind the truth here, as it truly stands and how it is.

sanskrit: śabdaḥ śrotraṃ tathā khāni trayam ākāśasaṃbhavam prāṇaś ceṣṭā tathā sparśa ete vāyuguṇās trayaḥ
english: Sound, hearing, and the bodily openings—these three arise from space. Breath, movement, and touch—these are the three qualities of wind.

sanskrit: rūpaṃ cakṣur vipākaś ca tridhā jyotir vidhīyate raso 'tha rasanaṃ sneho guṇās tv ete trayo 'mbhasām
english: Form, sight, and digestion—threefold is fire ordained. Taste, the tongue, and moisture—these are the three qualities of water.

sanskrit: ghreyaṃ ghrāṇaṃ śarīraṃ ca bhūmer ete guṇās trayaḥ etāvān indriyagrāmo vyākhyātaḥ pāñcabhautikaḥ
english: Smell, the nose, and the body—these are the three qualities of earth. Thus is the whole company of the senses, sprung from the five elements, explained.

sanskrit: vāyoḥ sparśo raso 'dbhyaś ca jyotiṣo rūpam ucyate ākāśaprabhavaḥ śabdo gandho bhūmiguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Touch belongs to wind, taste to water, form is said to belong to fire; sound has its origin in space, and smell is held to be the quality of earth.

sanskrit: mano buddhiś ca bhāvaś ca traya ete ''tmayonijāḥ na guṇān ativartante guṇebhyaḥ paramā matāḥ
english: Mind, intellect, and the inner disposition—these three are born of the Self's own source; they do not transcend the qualities, yet are held to be higher than the qualities.

sanskrit: indriyāṇi nare pañca ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu mana ucyate saptamīṃ buddhim evāhuḥ kṣetrajñaṃ punar aṣṭamam
english: In man there are five senses; the mind is reckoned the sixth; the intellect, they say, is the seventh; and the knower of the field is the eighth.

sanskrit: cakṣur ālocanāyaiva saṃśayaṃ kurute manaḥ buddhir adhyavasānāya sākṣī kṣetrajña ucyate
english: The eye is for mere seeing, the mind raises doubt, the intellect serves for resolve, and the knower of the field is said to be the witness.

sanskrit: rajas tamaś ca sattvaṃ ca traya ete svayonijāḥ samāḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tadguṇeṣūpalakṣayet
english: Passion, darkness, and goodness—these three are sprung from their own source, present alike in all beings; one should discern them by their respective signs.

sanskrit: yathā kūrma ihāṅgāni prasārya viniyacchati evam evendriyagrāmaṃ buddhiḥ sṛṣṭvā niyacchati
english: As the tortoise here stretches forth its limbs and draws them in again, so the intellect, having sent forth the company of the senses, draws them back.

sanskrit: yad ūrdhvaṃ pādatalayor avāṅmūrdhnaś ca paśyati etasminn eva kṛtye vai vartate buddhir uttamā
english: That which it sees above the soles of the feet and below the crown of the head—in just this task does the highest intellect engage.

sanskrit: guṇān nenīyate buddhir buddhir evendriyāṇy api manaḥṣaṣṭhāni sarvāṇi buddhyabhāve kuto guṇāḥ
english: The intellect leads on the qualities; the intellect leads the senses too, all of them with the mind as the sixth; and where the intellect is absent, whence then the qualities?

sanskrit: tatra yat prītisaṃyuktaṃ kiṃ cid ātmani lakṣayet praśāntam iva saṃśuddhaṃ sattvaṃ tad upadhārayet
english: Therein, whatever one marks within oneself as joined with gladness, serene as it were and wholly pure—that one should understand to be goodness.

sanskrit: yat tu saṃtāpasaṃyuktaṃ kāye manasi vā bhavet rajaḥ pravartakaṃ tat syāt satataṃ hāri dehinām
english: But whatever arises in the body or the mind joined with torment—that should be passion, the impeller, forever carrying embodied beings away.

sanskrit: yat tu saṃmohasaṃyuktam avyaktaviṣayaṃ bhavet apratarkyam avijñeyaṃ tamas tad upadhāryatām
english: But whatever is joined with bewilderment, whose object is unmanifest, beyond reasoning and not to be known—that should be understood to be darkness.

sanskrit: praharṣaḥ prītir ānandaḥ sāmyaṃ svasthātmacittatā akasmād yadi vā kasmād vartate sāttviko guṇaḥ
english: Exultation, gladness, joy, evenness, a self-possessed and settled mind—arising whether without cause or with cause, such is the sattvic quality at work.

sanskrit: abhimāno mṛṣāvādo lobho mohas tathākṣamā liṅgāni rajasas tāni vartante hetvahetutaḥ
english: Conceit, falsehood, greed, delusion, and impatience—these are the marks of passion, and they arise whether with cause or without.
